title: Vulnerability evidence workflow + RBAC v2 & audit-log integration
body:
Summary:

This is a working note describing the proposed end-to-end workflow for vulnerability scanner ingestion, automated evidence collection, RBAC v2 mapping for triage actions, and audit-log export schemas to the SIEM. Goal: reduce manual evidence collection, ensure every remediation has verifiable artifacts in the audit log, and make exceptions auditable.

Why this doc exists:
- We have recurring gaps where remediation evidence (screenshots, package-lock blames, patch PRs) is missing from the security ticket.
- SIEM exports currently capture scanner alerts but not consistently the remediation signals (deploy/PR/rollback).
- RBAC v1 made it hard to map who approved exceptions; RBAC v2 introduces scoped roles and temporary elevation which we need to reflect in audit entries.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: internal scanner outputs (Snyk/Trivy/OSS-scan), dependency review notes, patch SLA enforcement, evidence artifacts and how they map into audit logs and SIEM indices. Also covers RBAC v2 attributes required for traceability.
- Not in scope: creating new scanner integrations (we assume connector exists), large infra changes to SIEM collectors.

High-level workflow (informal):
1) Scanner run -> creates findings in Vulnerability DB (VulnDB). Finding payload includes scanner_id, vuln_id, severity, affected_artifacts, first_seen, and evidence_url (temp).
2) Vuln triage ticket auto-created (SEC-Jira). Ticket inherits scanner payload and assigns to a triage queue.
3) Triage action: triager selects action: patch, suppress, accept-risk, or escalate. Each action maps to an RBAC v2 permission (triage:patch, triage:suppress, triage:accept). Temporary elevation flow available for triage:escalate with justification.
4) Remediation steps recorded as structured evidence entries attached to ticket (patch-PR URL, build-artifact SHA, deployment run ID, rollback-ID).
5) Evidence automation hooks copy structured artifacts to evidence-store (immutable, time-stamped) and emit an audit-log event with schema described below.
6) SIEM ingestion processes audit events and correlates scanner -> PR -> deploy -> alert-closure.

Scanner payload (examples and required fields):
- scanner: string (e.g., snyk, trivy)
- scanner_run_id: string
- finding_id: string (unique per scanner)
- vuln_cve: string | null
- severity: critical|high|medium|low|info
- affected_package: name@version or artifact-id
- affected_host_or_cluster: k8s/pod id or AMI
- first_seen: ISO8601
- evidence_url: presigned URL to raw scanner report (optional)

Minimal triage ticket fields we require (auto-populated):
- ticket_id (SEC-####)
- created_by (system)
- assigned_team
- assigned_person
- initial_severity
- sla_due_date (per patch SLA table)
- required_evidence: list (patch-PR, build-SHA, deployment-ID)

Patch SLA (recommended, rough thresholds):
- Critical (RCE, active exploit): 24 hours to mitigation action, 72 hours to full patch/rollback in prod
- High (auth bypass, data exposure): 72 hours to mitigation action, 7 days to patch
- Medium: 14 days to patch
- Low/Info: 30 days to review or document as accepted risk
Notes: "mitigation action" can be temporary mitigation (WAF rule, config change) and must be recorded as evidence.

RBAC v2 mapping for vulnerability actions (proposal):
- role: vuln-triager -> permissions: triage:read, triage:create, triage:update, triage:comment
- role: vuln-remediator -> permissions: remediations:create, remediations:update, remediations:close
- role: vuln-approver -> permissions: exceptions:approve, exceptions:revoke
- role: oncall-elevation -> permission: temporary:elevate with duration and audit reason

RBAC attributes that must be captured in audit logs for each action:
- actor_id: user email or service-id
- actor_role: role(s) at time of action (include temporary elevation flag true/false)
- action: verb (create_ticket, attach_evidence, approve_exception, close_ticket, link_pr, deploy)
- target: ticket_id or resource id (pod, host, repo)
- timestamp: ISO8601
- session_id: ephemeral session id to tie UI+API actions
- justification: free text for exceptions or temporary elevations (if applicable)
- request_id: unique request id from the front-end/back-end for tracing

Audit-log schema (JSON message example):
{ "schema_version": "1.1", "event_type": "vuln.remediation.evidence_added", "timestamp": "2026-02-27T18:22:00Z", "actor_id": "sarah@redwood.ai", "actor_role": "vuln-remediator", "action": "attach_evidence", "target": "SEC-9123", "evidence_type": "patch-pr", "evidence_url": "s3://evidence-store/immutable/2026/02/9123/patch-pr-334.json", "session_id": "sess-abc-123", "request_id": "req-ff-77", "justification": "backported patch to 2.1.x for customer-impacting bug" }

SIEM mapping and indexes (implementation notes):
- We will export audit events to the SIEM on an event_type basis. Recommended indices/namespaces: siem.vuln.audit, siem.vuln.scanner, siem.vuln.remediation
- Extracted fields for rules and dashboards: finding_id, vuln_cve, scanner, severity, ticket_id, evidence_type, actor_id, actor_role, deployment_id, build_sha, action
- Typical correlation rule example: if scanner.alert (severity=critical) AND no remediation evidence within 24h -> create pager alert to sec-oncall
- Use deterministic event IDs (hash of scanner_run_id + finding_id + event_type) to avoid duplication on replays.

Evidence artifacts (types we should collect automatically):
- patch-pr: PR url and merge commit sha
- build-artifact: build id and sha + registry digest
- deploy-run: pipeline id, deploy timestamp, cluster/pod ids
- config-change: firewall/WAF rule id, config diff (link to immutable blob)
- dependency-upgrade: dependency diff and lockfile snippet + CVE references

Automation hooks (sketch):
- On ticket update to "remediation_in_progress" -> run evidence collector worker. Collector does:
  - poll linked PRs for merge/CI status and store build SHA if present
  - snapshot relevant package-lock/pom.xml snippets and store in evidence-store
  - grab last successful deploy run id from CI and attach to ticket
  - emit audit event for each artifact attached

Exceptions and transient acceptances:
- Exception requests must use exceptions:request action and include required fields: affected_scope, risk_statement, compensating_controls, expiration_date, approver_id
- Approval must be recorded as an audit event that includes the approver's role at time of approval and the expiration_date
- Temporary elevations used to approve an exception must also be recorded with a separate audit event that includes the reason and auto-revoke timestamp

Remediation tracking & reporting (dashboard metrics):
- mean-time-to-mitigation (MTTM) by severity
- percent of tickets with complete evidence at closure
- patch velocity (number of patches merged per week) broken down by team
- exception churn (open vs expired exceptions)
- audit log completeness (fraction of ticket events with session_id + request_id)

Outstanding engineering tasks (short list):
- [ ] Add schema_version routing in audit-bridge so we can evolve events without breaking SIEM
- [ ] Add session_id propagation across UI -> API -> worker
- [ ] Update RBAC service to emit role snapshot on elevation
- [ ] Wire evidence-collector to S3 immutable bucket with retention policy and checksum verification
- [ ] Create a Splunk/Datadog ingest mapping PR that extracts the fields listed above

Operational runbooks (note on quick triage for critical exploits):
- If critical exploit detected and exploitability score >= threshold: auto-create SEC-CRITICAL incident and notify sec-oncall, add mitigation action and set SLA to 24h. Evidence collector runs every 15m for SEC-CRITICAL incidents.

Open questions for review:
- What is the canonical field for "deployment_id" across CI providers? (CircleCI build_number vs GitHub Actions run_id vs Jenkins build id) Suggest we normalize to provider:run_id format.
- How should we handle fuzzy evidence (e.g., config change that can't be tied to a single deploy)? Proposal: capture diff + hash and mark evidence_type: config-change with scope notes.
- Do we enforce a minimum evidence set at ticket closure in Jira? If so, which fields are mandatory?

Next steps / proposed immediate actions (next 2 sprints):
1) Finalize audit_log schema_version 1.1 and implement emitter in triage service (Evan + infra).
2) Quick prototype: evidence-collector that extracts PR merge commit and stores artifact in evidence-store (Sofia + platform-eng).
3) RBAC v2 small change: emit role snapshot on temporary elevation (Liam + auth team).
4) Draft SIEM ingest mapping and a basic correlation rule for critical -> no-evidence pager (Priya + s&c team).

Notes to reviewers: this is working text; please add concrete Jira references for any infra tasks and call out backwards compatibility concerns for audit consumers.

Appendix: Example event timeline for a critical vuln (illustrative):
- T0: scanner run (snyk): finding_id F-991 created -> scanner event emitted to siem.vuln.scanner
- T0+5m: SEC-9900 ticket created, assigned to infra-team
- T0+12h: triager marks remediation_in_progress and links patch PR -> evidence.attach event emitted
- T0+20h: PR merged, CI published build sha -> evidence.build-published event emitted
- T0+27h: deploy job run -> evidence.deploy event emitted with deployment_id=github:actions:run-1357
- T0+28h: ticket closed -> remediation.closed event emitted

If anything below needs to be broken out into separate epics (e.g., schema migration vs evidence-store infra), flag here and we'll split in planning.
